okay i still have thoughts and no this isn’t personal criticism
just like my thoughts on the game structure
sorry it’s long tho so like genuinely take ur time
and wait till ur not busy
the way i see it, we were given a tribal explanation for what would happen and we went into playing immunity with that expectation in mind

we played an immunity competition that is fully dependent on risk assessment and what we’d do for immunity (part of the variables being measured would be what tribal were going to and the dynamics that would be in place)

i explained myself in my cfs my reasoning. i said at first i would probably go all the way (or at least super deep) but i figured with the way dallas was talking to me saying he wasn’t gonna be around for tribal and begging that we talk about a name before the challenge deadline, i could tell he was probably gonna be exiled the whole tribal. i didnt feel the need to risk forcing myself to go to at the very least EXILE for a shot of winning the comp. why would i purposely give myself punishments for less than an exile knowing im probably losing the comp anyways. plus dallas is my ally so i dont want to go past exile and risk me or him exiled through tribal unimmune.

the comp is literally designed for all (or almost all) or nothing so i feel that blaming the cast for abstaining isn’t a reflection of them being unwilling to have fun or participate. it’s just logical to either abstain or go hard in it? if you wanted people to do the comp for participation and fun’s sake, it could’ve been designed to “earn points” by taking punishments rather than needing to go in order down the list.

and then afterwards changing the layout to being a joint makes no sense at all. because that’s a massive shift in dynamic expectations for tribal council. and like i said before in a risk assessment competition “what would you do for immunity” part of it is what would you do for immunity… in a single tribal in your tribe. NOT what would you do for immunity in a joint tribal council situation.

i can sort of understand in some way that forcing the undead to go through the process of a tribal council is important for the game development, but looking at it strictly numbers and game structure wise that’s an unfair decision given the rest of the variables i said above. and it wouldn’t have been a real tribe immunity for them because they still lost stephen. and they’re obviously entering the joint with a numbers disadvantage. yes it’s frustrating to have a soft walk from stephen who broke the competition design but so many things could’ve been prevented and the call to make it a joint on top of being told yall basically just don’t care about how the calls made us feel just made things even worse
-Fio‼️ @perma5toned 03/25/2026 06:16 PM
so as far as the challenge goes, with a vast majority of players choosing to do zero tasks it ultimately meant that everyone was objectively willing to be vulnerable tonight for tribal. the premise of the round was that everyone would attend a tribal here and i wanted to stay true to the principle that this round and the correlating competition were designed for, which led to the decision to make the tribal a joint. would this decision have been made at say, f22? absolutely not - at this point in the season, players have had a lottt of time to 1. connect with the people they share tribes with, and 2. chances to meet everyone via safari and through player vc which do make the circumstances of a joint tribal more valid considering it’s not half the players here at this tribal are strangers you’re meeting for the first time

i completely recognize and take accountability for a joint tribal not being a perfect solution, it comes with its pros and cons but in my eyes it solves the big problem of this round’s planned double being completely ruined by stephen failing to follow through with the punishments he accepted. to be blunt, i put syn in charge of the challenge, they did a great job but things did not go as planned and my solution here is my attempt of trying to mitigate that in a way that
- makes bazz’s hard-earned individual immunity on villains still worth something instead of completely useless due to a tribal being rendered useless
- ensures that six of the ten people who scored a 0/10, and by proxy were willing to be vulnerable at tribal tonight, are still vulnerable at tribal
- levels the playing field between garden and undead by making it to where either tribe could have someone voted out, instead of unfairly punishing garden completely guaranteeing someone goes home while undead gets off scot free

i see through the perspectives of you and soul how this in a sense spoils the luck aspect of survivor although i disagree with the principle. in this game, luck is a factor that is bound to come up at a few different points, but i felt as if in recent instances that it would result in completely unfair outcomes - for starters, after the kebab walk, the decision to not swap back to garden/undead and let another old/new school round play out was in the exact same rationale as this round’s decision to transition to a joint tribal. because f16/f15 was always going to be a double elimination episode, old school’s earned tribe-immunity win is essentially completely negated as they would have been forced to attend another tribal no matter what.

this all boils down to a difference in game philosophy and difference in opinion on what is most fair, and in this instance there appears to be a very clear split between what the players see fit and what i see fit, as the host i have to make calls that are going to always be viewed in a split manner via public opinion. in recent situations, there has not ever been a “one solution solves all problems”. for people like you that have problems im willing to have calm discussions like this but for some people on this cast that i will not namedrop, i am not engaging with the level of entitlement and negative energy.

at this point, it is far too late to go back on calls and make any additional changes. i think in retrospect, the one thing i would have done differently is potentially provide another alternative method of earning individual immunity given the nature of a spontaneous joint tribal (will say is this is not the first time there has been a surprise joint tribal - in s2 we had a twist where i said two tribes lose but never specified it’s separate tribals and it then led to be a joint.. and in s4 no one successfully claimed greed within the allotted time which led to a joint tribal) the only problem with that is it goes back to undermining the results of the initial immunity challenge which makes it unfair to those who took punishments and WON via taking those punishments
again is it a perfect solution? no it is not, you and other players absolutely have the right to be frustrated, but understanding difference in philosophy is a two way street - i have always made an effort to see and understand the perspective of the players and i feel/felt through this that there was zero effort by the players to understand my perspective as the main host. recently this season has undoubtedly been a shitshow, i absolutely anticipate things will get better - part of that is absolutely my fault and as a result i will be making further efforts to bounce the momentum of the season and get us to a fun point again. just please bear with me and trust there is a method to my madness
